MEMORANDUM OF ARGUMENT (FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT, NOT A REAL FILING)

Applicant: Mr. R. Example
Respondent: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration

PART I - OVERVIEW

1. The Applicant seeks judicial review of a decision of the Refugee Protection Division that his refugee protection has ceased under paragraph 108(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27 (IRPA). The application is brought under section 72 of the IRPA and section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7.

2. The decision is reviewed on the reasonableness standard: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 at paras 10, 99.

PART II - FACTS

3. The Applicant, a citizen of India, was recognized as a Convention refugee in 2014. In 2022 he renewed his Indian passport to attend a family funeral and travelled to India for nine days.

4. The Minister applied to cease his protection under subsection 108(2) of the IRPA. The Member found that he had voluntarily reavailed himself of the protection of India and allowed the Minister's application.

PART III - ISSUES

5. Did the Member unreasonably find that the Applicant intended to reavail himself of the protection of India?

6. Did the Member breach procedural fairness by relying on evidence the Applicant was not shown?

PART IV - LAW AND ARGUMENT

7. The Member's reasons must be justified, intelligible and transparent: Vavilov, above at para 99. They must show that the Member grappled with the Applicant's explanation. Ibid at para 100.

8. Procedural fairness is assessed on the contextual factors in Baker v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [1999] 2 S.C.R. 817 at paras 21-28.

9. Courts give weight to a tribunal's findings of fact: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v. Khosa, 2009 SCC 12 at paras 59-62; Dunsmuir v. New Brunswick, 2008 SCC 9 at para 47. That deference does not excuse reasons that ignore the evidence.

10. The Member treated the passport renewal as conclusive. Intent is a question of fact, and a short visit for a family funeral points the other way. The Member's approach was inconsistent with the principle that hardship must be assessed in context: Kanthasamy v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 SCC 61 at paras 21-23, 33.

11. A recent decision of this Court confirms that a bare finding of reavailment, without reasons on intent, cannot stand: Smith v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2021 FC 999 at para 14. Subsection 108(1) of the IRPA does not make a passport renewal conclusive.

PART V - ORDER SOUGHT

12. The Applicant asks that the decision be set aside and the matter returned to a differently constituted panel.

steps.title: Welcome to the tour
steps.text: This short tour of iLIT will walk through some of the key features of the website. This is a live site walkthrough, not a pre-recorded demo. Press Next to move along, Back to go back, or Exit at any time.

steps.title: Let's begin in the research tab.
Search for a case
steps.text: This is the search bar, where research starts. We will begin with a simple search for a well known decision.

steps.title: Search results
steps.text: Search results display key information such as the citation, court, date, judge, outcome and how many decisions cite the case. Next, let's open some advanced search filters.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Filters are used in combination to narrow search results. Combine multiple selections to find specific case types. Clicking a filter will automatically search the library and display the results. Let's apply some filters: we will search for Refugee protection cases, won by the government, with the cessation and Sri Lanka tags.

steps.title: Filtered results
steps.text: We have {count} cases in the library that are classified as refugee protection, contain both the cessation and Sri Lanka tags, and were won by the government. Let's continue and open the top result, Veerasingam v. Canada.

steps.title: The reader
steps.text: This is the reader. It is comprised of three main sections, the header, the side panel, and the decision text.

steps.title: The decision
steps.text: The decision has been pulled from the FC Website, the text has been processed, and displayed in a formatted, easy to read way. iLIT marks what it has identified in the text with coloured highlights: case to case citations in gold, law and statute references in purple, and keyword tags in green. Let's continue, and see what a case to case citation looks like in the reader.

steps.title: Citations
steps.text: iLIT has connected every reference to its source in the database, meaning that users can see the text being referred to without leaving the site. Try hovering your mouse over the yellow highlighted Camayo citation to see the text preview.

steps.title: Citation cards
steps.text: Each citation can be expanded out, and opened as a paragraph in the decision. The pin icon keeps it from disappearing, the i icon will provide more information in the side panel. Let's move on to the side panel next.

steps.title: The side panel: About
steps.text: The side panel has three main sections. Feel free to scroll down to view each one more fully. The first section is called About. It sums up the case: the outcome, the decision maker, how many decisions cite it and what it cites, and the topics found in the text.

steps.title: The side panel: Authorities
steps.text: The Authorities tab groups and lists all citations and statutes that iLIT has identified within this decision. This can be used to navigate the decision.

steps.title: The side panel: Intelligence
steps.text: The final section of the side panel, Intelligence, has two subsections, Citation Intelligence, and Judge Profiles. Both default to the current case. Intelligence shows information from iLIT about how this case connects to others in the Library.

steps.title: The side panel: Judge Profiles
steps.text: The judge profile gives general insights into the decision maker for this decision.

steps.title: Explore the reader
steps.text: Feel free to spend a few minutes and explore the reader's functionality. When you are ready, click Next to proceed with the tour and continue to the main intelligence and statistics tabs.

steps.title: Next, Intelligence / Statistics
steps.text: Let's continue and open up the next main section of the website.

steps.title: Citation Intelligence
steps.text: This page is used to find the full citation intelligence features for decisions in the database. Let's return to a popular decision and search for Vavilov.

steps.title: Citation Intelligence
steps.text: This is the intelligence page for Vavilov. Feel free to scroll and take a look at the information available for this case. When ready, press Next to continue to Judge Profiles.

steps.title: Judge Profiles
steps.text: This page provides a profile for each Judge identified in the database by iLIT. Try for yourself, search for a name in the search box, and explore the profile of that Judge. When you are ready, press Next to continue to the next section.

steps.title: Next, FC Activity
steps.text: Let's continue to the FC Activity intelligence tab.

steps.title: FC Activity Analytics
steps.text:
This next tab sets iLIT apart from any other available platform out there. Every other site is built upon published decisions. However, the vast majority of cases we work with never reach a final decision. This is a huge blind spot when we are trying to get an understanding of the litigation landscape.

iLIT contains the FC Activity information of every single IMM case ever filed in the Federal Court. This information was pulled and collected, and is valuable in that it can provide additional context and statistics that no other site can. Feel free to scroll and view the charts. The filters above will change the charts below.

steps.title: Let's continue to the last major section of the website, the Analyst Workbench Demo.
The Analyst Workbench
steps.text: This feature is still in development. It will serve as a personal log in page, allowing users to track their live IMM number cases, pin case law decisions, and much more. You are now signed in to a demo account.

steps.title: Finally, we will finish off by exploring the most impactful use case for iLIT - the Live Analysis Feature.
Live Analysis
steps.text:
There are two important things to clarify before we continue.

1. iLIT today was built with the assistance of AI, but it does not run on it. The site works without relying on any external AI providers or third-party companies.

2. iLIT works by inputting plain text. What this means in practice is that **iLIT will work not just on court decisions, but on any inputted text.**

What this means is that iLIT can be used not just as a research tool for public decisions, but it can be used on any word document, or clearly legible PDF. And it can do it live, on the page, without storing anything permanently.

steps.title: A Word file, dropped in
steps.text: Let's demonstrate this functionality. We will drop in a made up word document and iLIT will process it, just like it has processed the 75k decisions in the database. The difference is, this process happens live, in memory, and the document is never saved by iLIT.

steps.title: A Word file, dropped in
steps.text: This is a fictional Memorandum of Argument from a refugee cessation judicial review, written for this demonstration. In practice it could be the memo filed by opposing counsel, or a draft an analyst is preparing.

steps.title: The memo, marked up
steps.text: iLIT went through the memo line by line. The counts show the case citations and statute references it found. Each one is marked in the text, as in the reader, so it can be previewed, opened as a card and pinned. A citation to a case in the library, such as Baker, links to that decision. This draft is not stored in the library, or added to the database in any way.

steps.title: Future use cases
steps.text: To be clear, this is just scratching the surface of how this feature, and iLIT as a whole, can benefit users. Check out the Coming soon section after the tour for more on the potential applications.

steps.title: That is the tour
steps.text: iLIT searches and reads Federal Court, Federal Court of Appeal and Supreme Court decisions, maps how they cite each other, profiles the judges, adds Federal Court activity data, and reads your own documents without saving them. The Workbench is still being built. Feel free to check out the 'see what is coming' section, or spend more time using the site.
